prs.title: Fix broken augmentExportEquals2 test fixture
prs.author: mahesh-desu
prs.body:
Fixes #64927.

The `augmentExportEquals2` conformance test fixture had a consecutive duplicate `// @filename: file3.ts` directive (line 18). The test harness saves the previous unit with empty content when it encounters a new `@filename` directive, then re-opens the same name — so the content-bearing `file3.ts` was wiped and the test silently expected **zero** errors.

Classic TypeScript (5.9.3 / 6.0) expects:

```
file2.ts(4,16): error TS2671: Cannot augment module './file1' because it resolves to a non-module entity.
file3.ts(3,8): error TS2503: Cannot find namespace 'x'.
```

**Change:** remove the duplicate `// @filename: file3.ts` line (1 line). This restores the full 3-file program and the expected diagnostics, matching the classic baselines exactly.

**Baselines:** new `augmentExportEquals2.errors.txt` + updated `.js` / `.types` / `.symbols`.

Credit to @ahejlsberg for diagnosing this on 2026-04-21: *"the test is broken. There are two `// @filename: file3.ts` in a row, which we apparently no longer handle."*

**Scope note:** this addresses only the `augmentExportEquals2` half of #63814. The `exportAssignmentMembersVisibleInAugmentation` spurious TS4060 regression and the `@types/node` `PlatformPath` augmentation failure remain open — both require deeper checker work.

Verified locally: full `hereby test` (no new failures), `hereby lint`, `hereby format`, `hereby check:format`, `hereby generate` (no diff).

prs.title: Add a default PGO profile for the compiler
prs.author: jakebailey
prs.body:
Let's give this a try again.

## PGO training

`default.pgo` is generated by the [Generate PGO profile](https://github.com/microsoft/typescript-benchmarking/blob/main/.github/workflows/pgo.yml) workflow in microsoft/typescript-benchmarking; this one came from [run 40764058553](https://github.com/microsoft/typescript-benchmarking/actions/runs/40764058553) against TypeScript `main` (equivalent to [`050fb369ee1`](https://github.com/microsoft/TypeScript/commit/050fb369ee1), which this branch has merged).

The workflow builds a non-PGO `noembed` compiler, then profiles one emit-enabled compilation of each compiler scenario that `perf test this faster` benchmarks, with diagnostic reporting disabled to avoid profiling forced garbage collections. The CPU profiles are merged with `go tool pprof -proto`, without normalization.

Scenarios: Compiler-Unions, angular-1, arktype, class-transformer, effect, mui-docs, sentry, social-app, strada-build-src, strada-compiler, t3code-server, tanstack-router, ts-pre-modules, vscode, webpack, xstate-main.

Scenario setup and configs are in [`cases/scenarios`](https://github.com/microsoft/typescript-benchmarking/tree/main/cases/scenarios); the emit overrides are in [`scripts/src/generatePgo.ts`](https://github.com/microsoft/typescript-benchmarking/blob/main/scripts/src/generatePgo.ts).

prs.title: Report an error for class declarations in statement position
prs.author: TimonGaertner
prs.body:
Fixes #22682

A class declaration used directly as the body of an `if`, `else`, loop, or labeled statement (for example `if (cond) class C {}`) is rejected by JavaScript engines with a `SyntaxError`, but `tsc` currently accepts it without any error, in both `.ts` and plain `.js` files. `interface` and `type` declarations in the same position already report TS1156 ("... declarations can only be declared inside a block").

This adds the same check to `checkClassDeclaration`, reusing `containerAllowsBlockScopedVariable`, so the class case reports:

```
error TS1156: 'class' declarations can only be declared inside a block.
```

Class expressions (`return class C {}`, `x = class C {}`) and class declarations in blocks, case clauses, namespaces, function bodies and at the top level are unaffected; the test covers these. TS1156 is already on the plain-JS diagnostic allowlist, so `.js` files get the error too.

Note: I limited this to `class`, following the clarified repro in the issue. `enum` in the same position is valid TypeScript (just useless, as noted in the issue), so I left it alone; happy to add it if wanted.

Test: new compiler test `classDeclarationInStatementPosition.ts`; no existing baselines change.

AI disclosure: I used Claude Code to help investigate the issue and write this change. I have reviewed and tested the result myself, understand it, and will handle the review discussion.

prs.title: Clarify error when content mapper extension ends in a built-in extension
prs.author: govardhanchinta99
prs.body:
Fixes #64917

A content mapper extension is rejected when it ends in a built-in extension (HasReservedSourceExtension does a suffix check). For `.const.json` the error said it "is a built-in extension", which is misleading, because `.const.json` is not built-in, it is rejected because it ends in `.json`.

This changes the message for TS18066 to: ```"Content mapper file extension '{0}' cannot be registered because it ends in a built-in extension."``` The error code and the check itself are unchanged. I did not add support for `.const.json`-style extensions, since that looks like a design decision for the team.

Changes:
- Reworded the message in diagnosticMessages.json
- Regenerated the dependent files with `npx hereby generate:diagnostics`
- Updated the renamed diagnostic variable in tsconfigparsing.go and its tests

Testing: the tsoptions package and the compiler test runner (internal/testrunner) pass, and `hereby check:format` is clean.

cc @andrewbranch, you worked on content mappers, so I'd appreciate your view on whether this wording works.

prs.title: Reuse token lookup visitor across AST descent
prs.author: Tom4ikss
prs.body:
`getTokenAtPosition` allocates a `NodeVisitor` and its hooks at each step down the tree. This change reuses one visitor for the duration of each lookup. Child and JSDoc traversal stay the same, and `VisitEachChildAndJSDoc` keeps its signature. Separate lookups still have separate visitors.

Profiling a tool that makes native API type queries showed repeated visitor allocations in token lookup. This patch did not produce a clear timing improvement in the full workload.

The benchmark looks up an identifier inside 24 nested calls. These are medians of five runs on Go 1.27.1 / darwin-arm64 / Apple M3 Pro:

| | Before | After |
|---|---:|---:|
| Time | 6.87 µs/op | 1.24 µs/op |
| Allocated bytes | 41,536 B/op | 1,664 B/op |
| Allocations | 153/op | 13/op |

The numbers cover this token lookup only. They do not measure overall compiler performance.

Validation on Node 24.22.1 and npm 11.19.1:
```sh
npx hereby generate
npx hereby validate --all
npx hereby test:benchmarks
npx hereby test:benchmarks:api
npm run -w @typescript/typescript build
npm run -w native-preview build
npx hereby check:format
```
All passed. The tidy checks for both Go modules and `go work sync` also passed, with a clean working tree afterwards.

To compare the benchmark with the parent revision, apply only the benchmark addition and run this from `tsc/`:
```sh
go test ./internal/astnav -run '^$' -bench BenchmarkGetTokenAtPositionNested -benchmem -count=5
```

Fixes #64929.

prs.title: Lint writes to protected record kind fields
prs.author: jakebailey
prs.body:
Node, type, and type mapper headers carry a kind that unsafe casts trust to identify the concrete allocation around the header. Assigning that kind, or copying a record by value, can leave a header that claims to be a larger record than its storage holds.

- Marks those kind fields with a `customlint:"protected"` struct tag. A new `protectedfield` analyzer rejects writes to protected fields (assignment, `++`/`--`, `&`, keyed or positional literals) and by-value copies, variables, parameters, results, and receivers of structs that contain one.
- The constructors that set a kind opt out with `//nolint:customlint`, so any new exception is visible in review. Casts already check the kind at runtime and kind zero is never valid, so zero-valued records cannot be cast into larger ones.
- The declarations transformer no longer clones a JS import declaration and retags its kind. It builds a real import declaration instead, with a new `importTag5` case. Tests that built bare node headers or retagged nodes now use the factory.

prs.title: Add wasip1 support, enabling CLI, API, browser, sync/async
prs.author: jakebailey
prs.body:
Fixes #63858
Fixes #63862
For #63813

This is still experimental, but it adds a `wasip1/wasm` build of `tsc`. The same `tsc.wasm` works two ways:

- **As a command.** Run it under any WASI host to get the CLI, LSP server, and so on.
- **As a reactor.** Instantiate it and hand it to the IPC-based JS API to get sync or async API access, including in the browser. This works similarly (though not identically) to David Sherret's ts-ast-viewer tsgo prototype.

The dual nature comes from some Wasm export and `binaryen` trickery that produces a single blob that can do both. In a perfect world we'd use wasip3 / the component model, but the main Go compiler can't do that yet.

This comes with a "no warranty" label for now: `tsc.wasm`, the wasip1 package, and the `typescript/wasm` host are all marked experimental and may change without notice.

## Packages

- **`@typescript/typescript-wasip1-wasm`** is an artifact-only package: `lib/tsc.wasm`, the `lib.*.d.ts` files beside it (like every other platform package), and `libFiles.json`. Install it at the same exact version as the main package.
- **`typescript/wasm`** in the main package owns the reactor host. It includes a minimal WASI shim, enough to make Go happy in browsers, and helpers (`instantiateWasm` / `instantiateWasmSync`) that produce a reactor instance for its `WasmTransport`. Custom transports can be plugged in through `typescript/sync/transport` and `typescript/async/transport`.
